lessons.title: Hundreds, tens and ones
lessons.art_alt: The castle guard waits by stacks of hundred, ten and one blocks

hook.text: The Place Value Castle gate opens with a magic number. Tonight the guard needs 243 blocks. Carrying 243 single blocks would take all night! Can you use the big blocks?
hook.say: The Place Value Castle gate opens with a magic number. Tonight the guard needs 243 blocks. Carrying 243 single blocks would take all night! Can you use the big blocks?

discover.text: Build the number with castle blocks. Drag a block onto the mat or tap it. Tap ➖ to take one back.
discover.hint: Start with the biggest blocks. How many hundreds? Then tens, then ones.
discover.say: Build the number with castle blocks. Drag a block onto the mat or tap it. Tap ➖ to take one back.

rule.text: In 243, the 2 means 2 hundreds, the 4 means 4 tens and the 3 means 3 ones. 200 + 40 + 3 = 243. A zero means none: 306 has no tens.
examples: Each place holds 0 to 9. Ten ones make a ten; ten tens make a hundred.
rule.say: In 243, the 2 means 2 hundreds, the 4 means 4 tens and the 3 means 3 ones. 200 plus 40 plus 3 equals 243. A zero means none: 306 has no tens.
sayEx: 243 equals 2 hundreds plus 4 tens plus 3 ones
306 equals 3 hundreds plus 0 tens plus 6 ones
Each place holds 0 to 9. Ten ones make a ten; ten tens make a hundred.

check.q: What is the digit 5 worth in 352?

notes.5: 5 is the digit, but it sits in the tens place, so it is worth 5 tens = 50.
notes.500: 500 would be 5 hundreds. In 352 the hundreds digit is 3.

check.explain: 352 = 3 hundreds, 5 tens, 2 ones. The 5 is worth 5 tens = 50.
check.say: What is the digit 5 worth in 352?

check.q: 4 hundreds, 0 tens and 7 ones make…

notes.470: 470 has 7 tens and 0 ones. We need 0 tens and 7 ones: 407.
notes.47: 47 has no hundreds. We need 4 hundreds: 407.

check.explain: Write a 0 for the empty tens place: 4 0 7 = 407.
check.say: 4 hundreds, 0 tens and 7 ones make…

check.q: Which number is 600 + 20 + 9?

notes.6209: Don't write 600, 20 and 9 side by side! 6 hundreds, 2 tens, 9 ones = 629.
notes.692: 692 swaps the tens and ones: it has 9 tens and 2 ones.

check.say: Which number is 600 plus 20 plus 9?

reteach.text: Here's another way. Think of money! A \$100 note, \$10 notes and \$1 coins. \$243 is two \$100 notes, four \$10 notes and three \$1 coins. The digits tell you how many of each.

discover.text: Build 125 with the blocks, like one \$100 note, two \$10 notes and five \$1 coins.
discover.hint: 1 hundred, 2 tens, 5 ones.
discover.say: Build 125 with the blocks, like one 100 dollar note, two 10 dollar notes and five 1 dollar coins.

reteach.say: Here's another way. Think of money! A 100 dollar note, 10 dollar notes and 1 dollar coins. 243 dollars is two 100 dollar notes, four 10 dollar notes and three 1 dollar coins. The digits tell you how many of each.

check2.q: In 718, what is the digit 1 worth?

notes.1: The 1 sits in the tens place, so it is worth 1 ten = 10.
notes.100: 100 would be the hundreds place. In 718 the hundreds digit is 7.

check2.explain: 718 = 7 hundreds, 1 ten, 8 ones. The 1 is worth 10.
check2.say: In 718, what is the digit 1 worth?

check2.q: 2 hundreds and 5 ones make…

notes.250: 250 has 5 tens. We need 0 tens and 5 ones: 205.
notes.25: 25 has no hundreds. We need 2 hundreds: 205.

check2.explain: No tens, so write 0 in the tens place: 205.
check2.say: 2 hundreds and 5 ones make…

check2.q: Which number is 300 + 40 + 8?

notes.3408: Don't write the parts side by side. 3 hundreds, 4 tens, 8 ones = 348.

check2.say: Which number is 300 plus 40 plus 8?

lessons.grown: 👪 MOE P2 Whole Numbers: numbers to 1000, place value (hundreds, tens, ones), number notation and expanded form.

lessons.title: Adding with regrouping
lessons.art_alt: The candy fairy beside a full gumdrop jar and bags of ten

hook.text: Gumdrop the candy fairy has 28 gumdrops and gets 15 more. Her ones jar can only hold 9 loose gumdrops. What happens when it gets too full?
hook.say: Gumdrop the candy fairy has 28 gumdrops and gets 15 more. Her ones jar can only hold 9 loose gumdrops. What happens when it gets too full?

discover.text: Move the new gumdrops into the ones jar. Drag them or tap them. When the jar has 10, bundle them into a ten-bag!
discover.hint: 10 loose gumdrops can become 1 ten-bag. Tap 🎀 Bundle when the jar has 10.
discover.say: Move the new gumdrops into the ones jar. Drag them or tap them. When the jar has 10, bundle them into a ten-bag!

rule.text: Add the ones first: 8 + 5 = 13 ones. Ten ones make 1 ten, so write 3 and carry 1 ten. Then add the tens: 2 + 1 + 1 = 4 tens. So 28 + 15 = 43.
rule.say: Add the ones first: 8 plus 5 equals 13 ones. Ten ones make 1 ten, so write 3 and carry 1 ten. Then add the tens: 2 plus 1 plus 1 equals 4 tens. So 28 plus 15 equals 43.
sayEx: 28 plus 15 equals 43 (8 plus 5 equals 13: write 3, carry 1)

notes.33: 6 + 7 = 13 ones. Carry the 1 ten: 3 tens + 1 ten = 4 tens, so 43.
notes.313: 13 ones is 1 ten and 3 ones. Carry the ten instead of writing 13: 43.

check.say: 36 plus 7 equals what?

check.q: In 47 + 25, the ones make 7 + 5 = 12. What do we write in the ones place?

notes.12: Only one digit fits in the ones place. 12 = 1 ten and 2 ones: write 2, carry 1.
notes.1: The 1 is the ten we carry to the tens. The ones digit is 2.

check.say: In 47 plus 25, the ones make 7 plus 5 equals 12. What do we write in the ones place?

notes.182: 4 + 8 = 12: write 2 and carry 1 ten. 5 + 3 + 1 = 9 tens. So 192.
notes.1812: Don't write 12 in the ones place; carry the 1 ten: 192.

check.say: 154 plus 38 equals what?

reteach.text: Here's another way: make a friendly ten! 28 is close to 30. Take 2 gumdrops from the 15 to make 30. Now 13 are left. 30 + 13 = 43. Same answer!

discover.text: Fill the jar to make a friendly ten, then bundle it!
discover.hint: The jar has 9. One more makes 10, then bundle!
discover.say: Fill the jar to make a friendly ten, then bundle it!

reteach.say: Here's another way: make a friendly ten! 28 is close to 30. Take 2 gumdrops from the 15 to make 30. Now 13 are left. 30 plus 13 equals 43. Same answer!

notes.13: 8 + 5 = 13 ones. Carry the 1 ten: 1 + 1 = 2 tens, so 23.
notes.113: 13 ones = 1 ten and 3 ones. Carry the ten: 23.

check2.say: 18 plus 5 equals what?

notes.313: Carry the ten instead of writing 13: 43.

check2.say: 29 plus 14 equals what?

check2.q: In 65 + 28, how many tens are there after carrying?

notes.8: 6 + 2 = 8 tens, plus the 1 ten carried from 5 + 8 = 13: 9 tens.

check2.say: In 65 plus 28, how many tens are there after carrying?

lessons.grown: 👪 MOE P2 Addition within 1000 with regrouping (carrying), with the 'make ten' mental strategy.

lessons.title: Times means equal groups
lessons.art_alt: Fairies dance around three mushroom fairy rings

hook.text: Tonight is the fairy dance! Every fairy ring needs the same number of mushrooms, or the magic won't work. Can you build the rings?
hook.say: Tonight is the fairy dance! Every fairy ring needs the same number of mushrooms, or the magic won't work. Can you build the rings?

discover.text: Make 3 fairy rings with 4 mushrooms in each. Drag a mushroom into a ring, or tap a ring to add one.
discover.hint: Every ring gets the same: 4 mushrooms each.
discover.say: Make 3 fairy rings with 4 mushrooms in each. Drag a mushroom into a ring, or tap a ring to add one.

rule.text: 3 groups of 4 is 4 + 4 + 4 = 12. We write it 3 × 4 = 12. The first number tells how many groups; the second tells how many in each group.
rule.say: 3 groups of 4 is 4 plus 4 plus 4 equals 12. We write it 3 times 4 equals 12. The first number tells how many groups; the second tells how many in each group.

check.q: 5 groups of 2 = ?

notes.5 + 2 = 7: That adds one 5 and one 2. 5 groups of 2 is 2 + 2 + 2 + 2 + 2 = 10.

check.say: 5 groups of 2 equals what?

check.q: Which one shows 3 × 5?

notes.5 bags with 5 sweets in each: That is 5 groups of 5 = 5 × 5. We need 3 groups.
notes.3 bags with 3 sweets in each: That is 3 × 3. We need 5 in each group.

check.say: Which one shows 3 times 5?

check.q: 4 fairy rings have 10 mushrooms each. How many mushrooms?
check.say: 4 fairy rings have 10 mushrooms each. How many mushrooms?

reteach.text: Here's another way: skip-count! Hop along a number line in jumps of the same size. 3 jumps of 4: 4… 8… 12! The number of jumps is the number of groups.

discover.text: Build 2 rings of 5 and count in 5s!
discover.hint: Each ring gets 5. Count: 5, 10.
discover.say: Build 2 rings of 5 and count in 5s!

reteach.say: Here's another way: skip-count! Hop along a number line in jumps of the same size. 3 jumps of 4: 4… 8… 12! The number of jumps is the number of groups.

check2.q: 2 groups of 3 = ?

notes.2 + 3 = 5: That adds 2 and 3. 2 groups of 3 is 3 + 3 = 6.

check2.say: 2 groups of 3 equals what?

check2.q: Which means 4 × 2?

notes.4 groups of 4: That is 4 × 4. We need 2 in each group.

check2.say: Which means 4 times 2?

check2.q: 3 plates have 5 cakes each. How many cakes?
check2.say: 3 plates have 5 cakes each. How many cakes?

lessons.grown: 👪 MOE P2 Multiplication: the concept of multiplication as equal groups (number of groups × number in each group), multiplication tables of 2, 3, 4, 5 and 10.

lessons.title: Sharing fairly
lessons.art_alt: Crumb the baker dragon brings cookies to four bear cubs

hook.text: Crumb the little baker dragon baked 12 cookies for four bear cubs. If one cub gets more than the others, there will be grumbles! Can you share them fairly?
hook.say: Crumb the little baker dragon baked 12 cookies for four bear cubs. If one cub gets more than the others, there will be grumbles! Can you share them fairly?

discover.text: Share the cookies so every plate gets the same. Drag a cookie to a plate, tap a plate, or tap Deal one each.
discover.hint: Give one cookie to each plate, then go round again until they're all gone.
discover.say: Share the cookies so every plate gets the same. Drag a cookie to a plate, tap a plate, or tap Deal one each.

rule.text: Sharing equally is dividing. 12 cookies shared among 4 plates is 3 each. We write 12 ÷ 4 = 3. Check with times: 4 × 3 = 12.
rule.say: Sharing equally is dividing. 12 cookies shared among 4 plates is 3 each. We write 12 divided by 4 equals 3. Check with times: 4 times 3 equals 12.

check.q: 12 stickers are shared equally between 2 children. How many does each child get?

notes.10: That's 12 − 2. Sharing means splitting into 2 equal groups: 6 and 6.
notes.14: Sharing makes each share smaller, not bigger. 12 ÷ 2 = 6.

check.say: 12 stickers are shared equally between 2 children. How many does each child get?

notes.5: 5 is the number of groups. Each group gets 4, because 5 × 4 = 20.
notes.15: That is 20 − 5. Sharing 20 into 5 equal groups gives 4.

check.say: 20 divided by 5 equals what?

check.q: 10 cupcakes are put on plates, 2 on each plate. How many plates are needed?

notes.2: 2 is how many go on each plate. Count the groups of 2 in 10: 5 plates.

check.say: 10 cupcakes are put on plates, 2 on each plate. How many plates are needed?

reteach.text: Here's another way: use times tables backwards! 12 ÷ 4 asks: 4 times what makes 12? 4 × 3 = 12, so each cub gets 3.

discover.text: Share 8 cookies between 2 plates. Then think: 2 times what makes 8?
discover.hint: Deal one each until they're gone.
discover.say: Share 8 cookies between 2 plates. Then think: 2 times what makes 8?

reteach.say: Here's another way: use times tables backwards! 12 divided by 4 asks: 4 times what makes 12? 4 times 3 equals 12, so each cub gets 3.

check2.q: 8 apples are shared equally among 4 friends. How many does each friend get?

notes.4: 4 is the number of friends. 4 × 2 = 8, so each gets 2.

check2.say: 8 apples are shared equally among 4 friends. How many does each friend get?

notes.10: 10 is the number of groups. 10 × 3 = 30, so each gets 3.

check2.say: 30 divided by 10 equals what?
18 divided by 3 equals what?

lessons.grown: 👪 MOE P2 Division: sharing equally and grouping, division as the inverse of multiplication (tables 2, 3, 4, 5, 10).

lessons.title: Halves, thirds and quarters
lessons.art_alt: The star fairy cuts a party pizza for her friends

hook.text: The star fairy is cutting a party pizza for her friends. If the slices aren't the same size, someone gets a tiny piece! How do we cut it fairly?
hook.say: The star fairy is cutting a party pizza for her friends. If the slices aren't the same size, someone gets a tiny piece! How do we cut it fairly?

discover.text: Slide to cut the pizza into equal slices, then tap the slices to colour them.
discover.hint: Quarters means 4 equal parts. Thirds means 3 equal parts.

stages.text: Cut the pizza into quarters (4 equal slices), then colour 1 slice.
stages.say: Cut the pizza into quarters (4 equal slices), then colour 1 slice.

stages.text: Now cut the chocolate bar into thirds (3 equal parts) and colour 2 parts.
stages.say: Now cut the chocolate bar into thirds (3 equal parts) and colour 2 parts.

discover.say: Slide to cut the pizza into equal slices, then tap the slices to colour them.

rule.text: 2 equal parts are halves, 3 equal parts are thirds, and 4 equal parts are quarters. In $\frac{1}{4}$, the bottom number tells how many equal parts there are; the top number tells how many we take.
rule.say: 2 equal parts are halves, 3 equal parts are thirds, and 4 equal parts are quarters. In the fraction one over four, the bottom number, four, tells how many equal parts there are. The top number, one, tells how many we take.
sayEx: one quarter equals one quarter , two thirds equals two thirds

check.q: A cake is cut into 4 equal pieces. One piece is…

notes.one half ($\\frac{1}{2}$): A half is one of 2 equal parts. This cake has 4 equal parts: a quarter.
notes.one third ($\\frac{1}{3}$): A third is one of 3 equal parts. This cake has 4: a quarter.

check.explain: 4 equal parts → each is one quarter, $\frac{1}{4}$.
check.say: A cake is cut into 4 equal pieces. One piece is…

check.q: Which shows halves?
options: a sandwich cut into 2 equal parts
a sandwich cut into 2 parts, one big and one small
a sandwich cut into 3 equal parts

notes.a sandwich cut into 2 parts, one big and: Halves must be EQUAL. A big part and a small part are not halves.
notes.a sandwich cut into 3 equal parts: 3 equal parts are thirds, not halves.

check.say: Which shows halves?

check.q: A bar has 3 equal parts and 2 parts are coloured. What fraction is coloured?

notes.$\\frac{1}{3}$: $\frac{1}{3}$ is one part. Two parts are coloured: $\frac{2}{3}$.
notes.$\\frac{3}{2}$: The bottom number is how many equal parts in all (3). The top is how many are coloured (2): $\frac{2}{3}$.

check.say: A bar has 3 equal parts and 2 parts are coloured. What fraction is coloured?

reteach.text: Here's another way: fold paper! Fold a strip in half once and you get 2 equal parts. Fold it in half again and you get 4 equal parts. The more equal parts, the smaller each part is.

discover.text: Fold the paper strip in half, then colour one half.
discover.hint: Halves means 2 equal parts.

stages.text: Cut the strip into halves (2 equal parts) and colour 1 part.
stages.say: Cut the strip into halves (2 equal parts) and colour 1 part.

discover.say: Fold the paper strip in half, then colour one half.

reteach.say: Here's another way: fold paper! Fold a strip in half once and you get 2 equal parts. Fold it in half again and you get 4 equal parts. The more equal parts, the smaller each part is.

check2.q: A pizza is cut into 3 equal slices. One slice is…

notes.one quarter ($\\frac{1}{4}$): A quarter is one of 4 equal parts. This pizza has 3: a third.
notes.one half ($\\frac{1}{2}$): A half is one of 2 equal parts. This pizza has 3: a third.

check2.explain: 3 equal parts → each is one third, $\frac{1}{3}$.
check2.say: A pizza is cut into 3 equal slices. One slice is…

check2.q: Which is bigger: $\frac{1}{2}$ or $\frac{1}{4}$ of the same pizza?

notes.$\\frac{1}{4}$: Cutting into 4 makes smaller slices than cutting into 2. A half is bigger.
notes.they are the same: Fold once for halves, twice for quarters: quarters are smaller. $\frac{1}{2}$ is bigger.

check2.explain: Fewer equal parts → bigger parts. $\frac{1}{2}$ is bigger than $\frac{1}{4}$.
check2.say: Which is bigger: one half or one quarter of the same pizza?

check2.q: A bar has 4 equal parts and 3 are coloured. What fraction is coloured?

notes.$\\frac{1}{4}$: $\frac{1}{4}$ is one part. Three parts are coloured: $\frac{3}{4}$.
notes.$\\frac{4}{3}$: The bottom number is the parts in all (4), the top is the coloured parts (3): $\frac{3}{4}$.

check2.say: A bar has 4 equal parts and 3 are coloured. What fraction is coloured?

lessons.grown: 👪 MOE P2 Fractions: fraction of a whole (halves, thirds, quarters), equal parts, notation, comparing unit fractions.

lessons.title: Subtracting with renaming
lessons.art_alt: Gumdrop unbundles a ten-bag of gumdrops on a candy bridge

hook.text: Gumdrop the candy fairy has 32 gumdrops on the candy bridge. A hungry duck takes 15. She only has 2 loose ones in her jar! How can she give the duck 5 ones?
hook.say: Gumdrop the candy fairy has 32 gumdrops on the candy bridge. A hungry duck takes 15. She only has 2 loose ones in her jar! How can she give the duck 5 ones?

discover.text: Take away 15 gumdrops. If the ones jar hasn't enough, tap 🎀 Unbundle to open a ten-bag into 10 ones. Then tap ➖ one or ➖ ten.
discover.hint: 2 ones aren't enough for 5. Unbundle one ten-bag first, then take ones, then tens.
discover.say: Take away 15 gumdrops. If the ones jar hasn't enough, tap 🎀 Unbundle to open a ten-bag into 10 ones. Then tap ➖ one or ➖ ten.

rule.text: When the ones aren't enough, rename a ten as 10 ones. 32 is 3 tens and 2 ones. Unbundle: 2 tens and 12 ones. Take 5 ones → 7 ones left. Take 1 ten → 1 ten left. So 32 − 15 = 17.
examples: 41 − 23: rename → 3 tens 11 ones, then take 3 ones and 2 tens → 18
rule.say: When the ones aren't enough, rename a ten as 10 ones. 32 is 3 tens and 2 ones. Unbundle: 2 tens and 12 ones. Take 5 ones, 7 ones left. Take 1 ten, 1 ten left. So 32 minus 15 equals 17.
sayEx: 32 minus 15 equals 17 (rename 3 tens 2 ones, 2 tens 12 ones)
41 minus 23: rename, 3 tens 11 ones, then take 3 ones and 2 tens, 18

notes.44: Ones: 2 is smaller than 8, so rename. 12 − 8 = 4 ones, and tens become 4 − 1 = 3. Answer 34.
notes.36: After renaming, ones are 12 − 8 = 4, not 6. Tens: 4 − 1 = 3 → 34.

check.say: 52 minus 18 equals what?

check.q: In 40 − 16, we rename because…
options: 0 ones are not enough to take 6

notes.4 tens are not enough: We have plenty of tens. The problem is the ones place: 0 < 6.
notes.40 is even: Being even doesn't decide renaming. We rename when the top ones digit is smaller.

check.explain: 0 ones < 6 ones, so open one ten: 3 tens and 10 ones, then subtract.
check.say: In 40 minus 16, we rename because…

check.q: After renaming 61 − 27, how many ones are on top?

notes.1: That was the ones digit before renaming. We borrow 1 ten → 11 ones.
notes.7: 7 is what we take away. After renaming the top ones become 11.

check.explain: 61 → 5 tens and 11 ones. Then 11 − 7 = 4 ones, 5 − 2 = 3 tens → 34.
check.say: After renaming 61 minus 27, how many ones are on top?

reteach.text: Here's another way: count up! From 15 up to 32. 15 → 20 is 5, 20 → 32 is 12. 5 + 12 = 17. Same answer, and you can check: 17 + 15 = 32.

discover.text: Take away 23. Unbundle if the ones jar needs more!
discover.hint: 1 one is less than 3. Unbundle a ten first.
discover.say: Take away 23. Unbundle if the ones jar needs more!

reteach.say: Here's another way: count up! From 15 up to 32. 15, 20 is 5, 20, 32 is 12. 5 plus 12 equals 17. Same answer, and you can check: 17 plus 15 equals 32.

check2.say: 70 minus 34 equals what?

notes.26: Taking away makes a smaller number. Rename: 1 ten 15 ones. 15 − 9 = 6, 1 ten left → 16.

check2.say: 25 minus 9 equals what?

check2.q: In 53 − 28, after renaming, the tens digit on top is…

notes.5: We borrowed one of those tens, so 5 becomes 4.
notes.2: 2 is what we take away from the tens. Top tens after renaming: 4.

check2.say: In 53 minus 28, after renaming, the tens digit on top is…

lessons.grown: 👪 MOE P2 Subtraction within 1000 with renaming (regrouping / borrowing), and checking by addition.

lessons.title: Dollars and cents
lessons.art_alt: Crumb counting dollar coins and cents at the bakery till

hook.text: Crumb the baker dragon's till needs \$1.25 for a jam tart. He has shiny \$1 coins, 10¢ coins and 1¢ coins. Can you count them onto the mat?
hook.say: Crumb the baker dragon's till needs 1 dollar and 25 cents for a jam tart. He has shiny 1 dollar coins, 10 cent coins and 1 cent coins. Can you count them onto the mat?

discover.text: Build each price with coins. Drag a coin onto the till or tap it. Tap ➖ to take one back.
discover.hint: Start with the biggest coins. How many \$1? Then 10¢, then 1¢.
discover.say: Build each price with coins. Drag a coin onto the till or tap it. Tap ➖ to take one back.

rule.text: Money uses place value too! \$1 is 100 cents, a 10¢ coin is 10 cents, and a 1¢ coin is 1 cent. \$1.25 = 1 × \$1 + 2 × 10¢ + 5 × 1¢. The dot separates dollars from cents.
rule.say: Money uses place value too! One dollar is 100 cents, a 10 cent coin is 10 cents, and a 1 cent coin is 1 cent. One dollar 25 is 1 dollar, 2 ten-cent coins and 5 one-cent coins. The dot separates dollars from cents.
sayEx: 1 dollar and 25 cents equals 1 times 1 dollar plus 2 times 10 cents plus 5 times 1 cent
2 dollars and 40 cents equals 2 times 1 dollar plus 4 times 10 cents

check.q: How many cents is \$1.30?

notes.103: The 3 is in the ones-of-cents place after a 0: 30 cents, not 3. 100 + 30 = 130.

check.say: How many cents is 1 dollar and 30 cents?
3 times 1 dollar plus 2 times 10 cents plus 4 times 1 cent equals what?

check.q: A bun costs 80¢. Which coins make exactly 80¢?

notes.8 × 1¢: That is only 8 cents. We need 80 cents: eight 10¢ coins.

check.say: A bun costs 80 cents. Which coins make exactly 80 cents?

reteach.text: Here's another way: think in cents first, then write the dollars. 240 cents = 2 dollars and 40 cents, written \$2.40. The last two digits are always the cents!

discover.text: Build \$1.05 with the coins.
discover.hint: 1 × \$1 and 5 × 1¢. No 10¢ coins.
discover.say: Build 1 dollar and 5 cents with the coins.

reteach.say: Here's another way: think in cents first, then write the dollars. 240 cents equals 2 dollars and 40 cents, written 2 dollars and 40 cents. The last two digits are always the cents!

check2.q: \$2.15 is how many cents?

notes.21.5: Don't treat the dot like a decimal you divide by. \$2.15 = 215 cents.
notes.2015: Just join 2 and 15 with the cents: 200 + 15 = 215.

check2.say: 2 dollars and 15 cents is how many cents?
1 times 1 dollar plus 5 times 10 cents plus 0 times 1 cent equals what?

check2.q: Which is more money?
check2.say: Which is more money?

lessons.grown: 👪 MOE P2 Money: dollars and cents, counting and making amounts, the decimal-point notation for money.

lessons.title: Five-minute clock
lessons.art_alt: A pastel fairy clock tower with a big round clock in soft evening light

hook.text: The fairy clock tower stopped at the wrong time! The lantern parade starts at 3:25. Can you move the hands to the right place?
hook.say: The fairy clock tower stopped at the wrong time! The lantern parade starts at 3:25. Can you move the hands to the right place?

discover.text: Set the clock. Tap 5 min ⏩ to move the long hand, and hour ⏩ for the short hand. You can also tap a number on the clock face for the minutes.
discover.hint: Count the long hand in fives: each number is 5 more minutes. 5 numbers past 12 → 25 minutes.
discover.say: Set the clock. Tap 5 min ⏩ to move the long hand, and hour ⏩ for the short hand. You can also tap a number on the clock face for the minutes.

rule.text: The long hand counts minutes in fives. On 1 → 5 minutes, on 2 → 10, on 5 → 25, on 8 → 40. The short hand points near the hour. So long hand on 5 and short hand just past 3 means 3:25.
rule.say: The long hand counts minutes in fives. On 1, 5 minutes, on 2, 10, on 5, 25, on 8, 40. The short hand points near the hour. So long hand on 5 and short hand just past 3 means 3:25.

check.q: The long hand points to 4. How many minutes?

notes.4: The number 4 is not 4 minutes. Count in fives: 5, 10, 15, 20.
notes.40: 40 minutes is the long hand on 8 (8 × 5 = 40). On 4 → 20.

check.say: The long hand points to 4. How many minutes?

check.q: What time is it when the short hand is just past 2 and the long hand is on 6?

notes.6:10: The short hand shows the hour (2). The long hand on 6 → 30 minutes: 2:30.
notes.2:06: Long hand on 6 is half past, 30 minutes — not 6 minutes.

check.explain: Long hand on 6 = 30 minutes. Short hand past 2 → 2:30.
check.say: What time is it when the short hand is just past 2 and the long hand is on 6?

check.q: The long hand on 9 means…

notes.90 minutes: A clock only goes to 60 minutes. 9 × 5 = 45.

check.say: The long hand on 9 means…

reteach.text: Here's another way: skip-count from the 12! Whisper 5, 10, 15, 20… as you pass each number with the long hand. Stop when you reach the number it points to.

discover.text: Set the clock to 7:15. Count in fives to the 3!
discover.hint: Long hand on 3 → 15 minutes. Short hand just past 7.
discover.say: Set the clock to 7:15. Count in fives to the 3!

reteach.say: Here's another way: skip-count from the 12! Whisper 5, 10, 15, 20… as you pass each number with the long hand. Stop when you reach the number it points to.

check2.q: Long hand on 2 means…

notes.20 minutes: 20 is the long hand on 4. On 2 → 10 minutes.

check2.say: Long hand on 2 means…

check2.q: Which time has the long hand on 8?

notes.4:08: 08 minutes would be just past the 1, not on 8. On 8 → 40 minutes.
notes.8:20: That would be short hand near 8 and long hand on 4. We need long hand on 8 → :40.

check2.say: Which time has the long hand on 8?

check2.q: Half past 5 is…

notes.5:15: Quarter past is :15 (long hand on 3). Half past is :30 (long hand on 6).
notes.6:30: Half past 5 is still in the 5 o'clock hour: 5:30.

check2.explain: Half past = 30 minutes = long hand on 6 → 5:30.
check2.say: Half past 5 is…

lessons.grown: 👪 MOE P2 Time: telling time to 5 minutes, hour and minute hands, o'clock / half past / quarter past and to.

lessons.title: Picture graphs with a key
lessons.art_alt: Festival parade with sticker pictures lining up in pastel rows

hook.text: The Picture Graph Parade is lining up stickers for each float! But the key says each sticker stands for 5 friends — not 1. Can you build the graph so the counts are right?
hook.say: The Picture Graph Parade is lining up stickers for each float! But the key says each sticker stands for 5 friends — not 1. Can you build the graph so the counts are right?

discover.text: Tap ➕ (or the row) to add a balloon sticker. Each 🎈 = 5. Match the numbers: Roses 15, Stars 10, Moons 20.
discover.hint: Roses need 15 ÷ 5 = 3 stickers. Stars 10 ÷ 5 = 2. Moons 20 ÷ 5 = 4.
discover.say: Tap ➕ (or the row) to add a balloon sticker. Each 🎈 equals 5. Match the numbers: Roses 15, Stars 10, Moons 20.

rule.text: In a picture graph with a key, one picture can stand for more than one. If each picture = 5, then 3 pictures mean 3 × 5 = 15. Always read the key first!
examples: Count pictures, then multiply by the key
rule.say: In a picture graph with a key, one picture can stand for more than one. If each picture equals 5, then 3 pictures mean 3 times 5 equals 15. Always read the key first!
sayEx: Count pictures, then multiply by the key

check.q: Key: each 🧁 = 2. A row has 4 cupcakes. How many?

notes.4: 4 is the number of pictures. Multiply by the key: 4 × 2 = 8.

check.say: Key: each 🧁 equals 2. A row has 4 cupcakes. How many?

check.q: Key: each 🌸 = 10. We need to show 30 flowers. How many pictures?

notes.10: 10 is the key, not the number of pictures. 30 ÷ 10 = 3 pictures.
notes.30: That would be if each picture = 1. With key 10: 30 ÷ 10 = 3.

check.say: Key: each 🌸 equals 10. We need to show 30 flowers. How many pictures?

check.q: Why do picture graphs use a key?
options: so one picture can stand for many

notes.to make the pictures prettier: Cute pictures are fun, but the key's job is to tell you the scale.
notes.so we never multiply: You do multiply (or divide)! The key tells you by how much.

check.explain: The key tells you the scale: each picture = 2, 5 or 10…
check.say: Why do picture graphs use a key?

reteach.text: Here's another way: think of skip-counting! If each sticker = 5, whisper 5, 10, 15 as you place the 1st, 2nd, 3rd sticker. Stop when you reach the number you need.

discover.text: Each ⭐ = 2. Build Apples = 8 and Bells = 6.
discover.hint: 8 ÷ 2 = 4 stars. 6 ÷ 2 = 3 stars.
discover.say: Each ⭐ equals 2. Build Apples equals 8 and Bells equals 6.

reteach.say: Here's another way: think of skip-counting! If each sticker equals 5, whisper 5, 10, 15 as you place the 1st, 2nd, 3rd sticker. Stop when you reach the number you need.

check2.q: Key: each 🎀 = 5. 2 ribbons show…

notes.5: 5 is the key for one picture. Two pictures → 10.

check2.say: Key: each 🎀 equals 5. 2 ribbons show…

check2.q: Key: each 🐸 = 10. How many pictures for 40 frogs?
check2.say: Key: each 🐸 equals 10. How many pictures for 40 frogs?

check2.q: A graph key says each picture = 1. Then 6 pictures mean…

notes.12: Only if the key were 2. Key 1 means each picture is one: 6.
notes.1: 1 is the key, not the total. 6 pictures × 1 = 6.

check2.say: A graph key says each picture equals 1. Then 6 pictures mean…

lessons.grown: 👪 MOE P2 Data Analysis: picture graphs with scales of 1, 2, 5 or 10; reading and building graphs.

lessons.title: Two-step bar stories
lessons.art_alt: Gingerbread baker with two trays of cookies, sold and fresh

hook.text: The Gingerbread Baker baked 50 cookies. He sold 20, then baked 15 more. The bar model can show both steps — take away, then add. Can you label it?
hook.say: The Gingerbread Baker baked 50 cookies. He sold 20, then baked 15 more. The bar model can show both steps — take away, then add. Can you label it?

discover.text: Drag or tap “sold 20” onto the sold part, then “+ 15” onto the new part.
discover.hint: Do the take-away first. Then join the new batch on the end of the bar.
discover.say: Drag or tap “sold 20” onto the sold part, then “+ 15” onto the new part.

rule.text: A two-step story needs two moves. First: 50 − 20 = 30 left. Second: 30 + 15 = 45 now. The bar shows the sold chunk, the left chunk, and the new chunk joined on.
examples: Check: sold + left = start, left + new = now
rule.say: A two-step story needs two moves. First: 50 minus 20 equals 30 left. Second: 30 plus 15 equals 45 now. The bar shows the sold chunk, the left chunk, and the new chunk joined on.
sayEx: Check: sold plus left equals start, left plus new equals now

check.q: Mia had 40 stickers, gave away 12, then got 8 more. How many now?

notes.28: That's only the first step (40 − 12). Then add 8: 28 + 8 = 36.
notes.48: That's 40 + 8 without giving any away. Do both steps: 40 − 12 + 8 = 36.

check.say: Mia had 40 stickers, gave away 12, then got 8 more. How many now?

check.q: In a bar model for “sold then baked more”, the first part you mark is…

notes.the new batch only: Add comes second. Mark the sold take-away first so “left” is clear.
notes.the answer only: The bar helps you find the answer; you build the parts first.

check.explain: Take away first, then join the new part.
check.say: In a bar model for “sold then baked more”, the first part you mark is…

check.q: A baker baked 35 buns, sold 10, baked 6 more. How many now?
check.say: A baker baked 35 buns, sold 10, baked 6 more. How many now?

reteach.text: Here's another way: write a number sentence with two signs. Start − sold + new = now. Fill the numbers, then work left to right.

discover.text: Label the bar: sold 12, then + 8.
discover.hint: Take away 12 first, then add 8.
discover.say: Label the bar: sold 12, then plus 8.

reteach.say: Here's another way: write a number sentence with two signs. Start minus sold plus new equals now. Fill the numbers, then work left to right.

check2.q: Sam had 28 marbles, lost 9, then found 5. How many now?
check2.say: Sam had 28 marbles, lost 9, then found 5. How many now?

check2.q: Which number sentence matches: baked 60, sold 25, baked 10 more?

notes.60 + 25 − 10: Sold means take away, not add. New batch is + 10.
notes.60 − 25 − 10: The new batch is added, not taken away.

check2.say: Which number sentence matches: baked 60, sold 25, baked 10 more?

check2.q: After 18 − 7 + 4, what is the answer?
check2.say: After 18 minus 7 plus 4, what is the answer?
